skill.name: cc-devflow-orchestrator
skill.description: Routes CC-DevFlow users to the right workflow command, agent, and phase gate for project and requirement delivery.
skill.summary: Routes CC-DevFlow project, requirement, review, QA, and troubleshooting workflows.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backtick false positives around slash-command documentation, not Ruby or shell execution. Three findings are confirmed because the skill tells users to run local shell scripts under .claude/scripts; these fixed-path commands require review before execution.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running each .claude/scripts shell command, and tell users to inspect the script first.

remediation.issue: Unclear trust boundary for referenced project assets
remediation.suggestion: State that referenced agents, commands, rules, and scripts must be reviewed in the local project before use.

remediation.issue: Slash commands can look like shell commands to scanners
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that /flow-* and /core-* entries are Claude Code slash commands, not operating system commands.

static_findings.snippet: - `/flow-init` 包含 Brainstorming 阶段,生成 BRAINSTORM.md 作为需求「北极星」
- `/flow-prd` 需要 BRAINSTORM.md 对齐检查
- `/flow-clarify` 在 PRD 前可选执行,消除 research.md 中的歧义
- `/flow-epic` 使用 bite-sized tasks 原则 (2-5分钟/任务)
- `/flow-dev` 默认 Autonomous 模式(自动重试),使用 `--manual` 退出到 Manual 模式
- `/flow-review` 是新增的两阶段审查 (Spec Compliance → Code Quality)
- `/flow-ui` 和 `/flow-dev` 自动加载 `devflow/STYLE.md`(如存在)
- **DO**: Recommend `/flow-qa` command → invokes qa-tester + security-reviewer agents
- **DO**: Recommend `/flow-review` command → invokes spec-reviewer + code-quality-reviewer agents
- `/flow-fix "BUG-123|登录超时"` - 系统化 BUG 修复 (4阶段调试法)
**Rationale**: Avoid duplication ("不重不漏" principle). Agents and Commands own detailed standards.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time choosing the next CC-DevFlow command during complex delivery work. This skill maps project status, phase gates, and user intent to the right Claude, Codex, or Claude Code workflow.
actual_capabilities: Maps project-level workflows to roadmap, architecture, guidelines, and style commands.
Routes requirement workflows from flow-init through release and verification.
Recommends agents for clarification, PRD, design, planning, QA, and review tasks.
Uses orchestration status states to suggest the next workflow command.
Provides troubleshooting routes for missing documents, phase gates, and constitution checks.
Lists auxiliary commands for status, upgrade, bug fix, and code review work.
limitations: It does not implement the referenced flow commands or agents.
It assumes CC-DevFlow command files, agents, scripts, and rules exist in the project.
Some guidance references local shell scripts that require trust review before use.
It does not replace detailed phase gate validation or constitution rules.

use_cases.title: Start a new requirement workflow
use_cases.description: Identify the right first command and expected documents for a new feature request.

use_cases.title: Resume an interrupted delivery phase
use_cases.description: Use the current orchestration status to select the next command without repeating completed work.

use_cases.title: Route review and release checks
use_cases.description: Choose the correct review, QA, verification, and release commands near the end of delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Pick the first workflow command
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: starting a new feature or requirement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cc-devflow-orchestrator to choose the first CC-DevFlow command for this requirement. Explain the expected document outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Find the next phase command
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: continuing from a known workflow status.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cc-devflow-orchestrator with my current orchestration status. Recommend the next command and any optional alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Route review and QA work
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: development is complete and quality gates are next.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cc-devflow-orchestrator to decide whether I should run review, QA, verification, or release next. Include the responsible agents.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a blocked workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: a phase gate or missing document blocks progress.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cc-devflow-orchestrator to diagnose this blocked CC-DevFlow workflow. Recommend the recovery path and any files or scripts to inspect first.

output_examples.input: I finished research and need to create product requirements.
output_examples.output: Recommended next step: run the PRD workflow. Confirm the brainstorming document exists and aligns with the research notes first.

output_examples.input: The status says development is complete. What comes next?
output_examples.output: Recommended next step: run the two-stage review workflow. QA is an alternative only when review is intentionally skipped.

output_examples.input: A phase gate failed because a required document is missing.
output_examples.output: Recommended next step: check the orchestration status, identify the incomplete phase, and generate a status report after reviewing the local script.

best_practices: Confirm the current orchestration status before following any routing recommendation.
Review referenced command, agent, and rule files when detailed standards matter.
Ask for explicit approval before running any referenced local shell script.
anti_patterns: Treating this orchestrator as the source of detailed implementation standards.
Running suggested local scripts without inspecting their contents and trust boundary.
Skipping phase gates because the next command appears obvious.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It routes CC-DevFlow users to the right workflow command, agent, and phase gate reference.

faq.question: Does it create requirements or code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It points to the commands and agents that perform those tasks.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed around Claude Code slash commands and related CC-DevFlow agents.

faq.question: Does it work without the rest of CC-DevFlow?
faq.answer: Only as a reference. The referenced commands, agents, rules, and scripts must exist locally.

faq.question: Why does the audit mention shell scripts?
faq.answer: The skill tells users to run local scripts for troubleshooting and validation. Review those scripts before execution.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you know the delivery context but need the next CC-DevFlow command or responsible agent.
